section: Coal sector - reserves, production, washing, commercial mining, coal gasification
subsections: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme
Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity
Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: In coal gasification, coal is converted into syngas by partial oxidation with which of the following at high temperature and pressure?
accepted.x: Coal is partly oxidised with oxygen and steam at high temperature and pressure to produce syngas.
accepted.tq: Identify the process inputs rather than the products.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a constituent of the syngas produced through coal gasification?
accepted.x: Syngas is a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide. Ammonia is a product that can be manufactured using syngas, not a stated constituent of syngas.
accepted.tq: Separate the composition of syngas from products made using syngas.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following products can be manufactured using coal gasification?
1. Synthetic natural gas
2. Methanol
3. Ammonia for fertilisers
4. Dimethyl ether
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Coal gasification can produce synthetic natural gas, methanol, ammonia for fertilisers, hydrogen, dimethyl ether, ammonium nitrate and petrochemicals.
accepted.tq: Use the complete product list to identify the all-inclusive combination.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: Syngas produced through coal gasification can also be used to operate which of the following power-generation systems?
o: Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle power plants
accepted.x: Syngas can be used to run Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle (IGCC) power plants.
accepted.tq: Match the specialised fuel product with its stated power-generation application.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following substances:
1. Ethanol
2. Nitroglycerine
3. Urea
Which of the substances listed above can be produced through coal gasification?
accepted.x: Ethanol and urea can be produced through coal gasification. Nitroglycerine is not included among the stated products.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between direct gasification products and an unrelated chemical.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: The National Coal Gasification Mission aims to gasify how much coal by 2030?
accepted.x: The National Coal Gasification Mission has a target of gasifying 100 million tonnes of coal by 2030.
accepted.tq: Recall the mission target and distinguish it from the sub-target under the incentive scheme.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: What was the outlay approved for the Coal Gasification Incentive Scheme introduced in 2024?
accepted.x: The Coal Gasification Incentive Scheme of 2024 has an outlay of ₹8,500 crore for public and private projects.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the outlay of the 2024 scheme from the later surface coal and lignite scheme.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification, consider the following statements:
1. It was approved by the Cabinet on 13 May 2026.
2. Its outlay is ₹37,500 crore.
3. The incentive may be up to 20% of plant and machinery cost.
4. The incentive is capped at ₹5,000 crore per project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the scheme approved on 13 May 2026, including its outlay, incentive rate and project-wise ceiling.
accepted.tq: Check the date, outlay, percentage and cap as separate components of one scheme.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification is intended to contribute approximately how much coal gasification capacity towards the 100-million-tonne mission target?
accepted.x: The scheme targets about 75 million tonnes of coal gasification capacity towards the 100-million-tonne mission goal.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the scheme contribution from the overall mission target.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification, the coal linkage tenure was extended to:
accepted.x: The coal linkage tenure under the scheme was extended to 30 years.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact duration of the policy provision.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the status of the ₹37,500-crore coal gasification scheme?
o: Bidding was permanently closed after one unsuccessful round.
All eligible projects had already received the incentive.
The scheme was withdrawn because the mission target had been achieved.
No bidders had turned up, and bid windows were planned every two months.
accepted.x: No bidders had turned up for the scheme, and bid windows were planned at intervals of two months.
accepted.tq: Use the current-status detail rather than confusing it with scheme approval or implementation.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: The import bill for substitutable products such as LNG, urea, ammonia, coking coal, methanol and DME was approximately what amount in FY2025?
accepted.x: The import bill for these substitutable products was about ₹2.77 lakh crore in FY2025.
accepted.tq: Read the unit carefully and distinguish lakh crore from crore figures.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the only commercial-scale coal gasification plant identified in the sector?
o: The Talcher fertiliser plant in Odisha
MCL's IB Valley Washery in Odisha
accepted.x: JSPL's plant at Angul, Odisha, is identified as the only commercial-scale coal gasification plant.
accepted.tq: Match the project with its distinctive status and location.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: The first gasification-based fertiliser plant at Talcher is due to be completed by:
accepted.x: The first gasification-based fertiliser plant at Talcher is due by December 2027.
accepted.tq: Recall the project timeline without confusing it with the mission target year.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about BCGCL:
1. It is a joint venture of BHEL and CIL.
2. It was formed on 21 May 2024.
3. It is building a commercial coal-to-ammonium-nitrate plant at Lakhanpur in Jharsuguda district.
4. The plant is located in Odisha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: BCGCL is a BHEL-CIL joint venture formed on 21 May 2024, and it is constructing the plant at Lakhanpur, Jharsuguda, Odisha.
accepted.tq: Verify the organisation, formation date, project and location independently.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Lakhanpur coal-to-ammonium-nitrate plant being built by BCGCL is designed for which of the following capacities?
o: 2,500 TPD of coal input and 2,000 TPD of ammonium nitrate output
2,000 TPD of coal input and 2,500 TPD of ammonium nitrate output
2,000 TPD each of coal input and ammonium nitrate output
2,500 TPD each of coal input and ammonium nitrate output
accepted.x: The plant is designed to use 2,500 tonnes per day of coal and produce 2,000 tonnes per day of ammonium nitrate.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing input and output figures in a capacity question.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: Commercial coal blocks receive a 50% rebate on revenue share when at least what proportion of their output is used for gasification?
accepted.x: A 50% rebate on revenue share is available when at least 10% of the commercial block's output is used for gasification.
accepted.tq: Separate the rebate percentage from the qualifying output percentage.
accepted.sec: Coal gasification - syngas products, mission target, incentive scheme  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Indian coal?
o: High ash, high calorific value, low ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
High ash, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and low sulphur
Low ash, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
Low ash, high calorific value, low ash-fusion temperature and high sulphur
accepted.x: Indian coal generally has high ash content, low calorific value, high ash-fusion temperature and low sulphur content.
accepted.tq: Track all four quality characteristics without reversing paired properties.
accepted.sec: Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity  [other exams]

accepted.s: The ash content of Indian coal is generally in which range?
accepted.x: Indian coal is characterised by a high ash content of approximately 35–45%.
accepted.tq: Recall the stated range and reject lower, more typical-quality coal figures.
accepted.sec: Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity  [other exams]

accepted.s: The sulphur content of Indian coal is approximately:
accepted.x: Indian coal generally has low sulphur content of about 0.5%.
accepted.tq: Use the decimal carefully; the major trap is a tenfold change in magnitude.
accepted.sec: Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a problem affecting the Indian coal sector?
o: Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal
accepted.x: The identified problems include poor quality, movement bottlenecks, low washery use, rising coking-coal imports and administrative issues. Excessive availability of high-quality domestic coking coal is not a stated problem.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the sectoral problem described.
accepted.sec: Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity  [other exams]

accepted.s: Disruption of thermal power generation due to rail and logistics delays primarily reflects which problem in the coal sector?
accepted.x: Rail and logistics delays create movement and evacuation bottlenecks, which can disrupt thermal power generation.
accepted.tq: Translate the practical situation into the underlying sectoral problem.
accepted.sec: Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity  [other exams]

accepted.s: Coking coal is imported mainly from which country, while non-coking coal is obtained mainly from Indonesia and South Africa?
accepted.x: Coking coal is imported mainly from Australia, whereas non-coking coal comes mainly from Indonesia and South Africa.
accepted.tq: Keep the source countries of coking and non-coking coal separate.
accepted.sec: Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity  [other exams]

accepted.s: APGENCO procures washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery for which of the following power stations or units?
o: RTPP 600 MW and Dr NTTPS 500/800 MW units
RTPP 500 MW and Dr NTTPS 600/1000 MW units
accepted.x: APGENCO buys washed coal from MCL's IB Valley Washery for the 600 MW RTPP and the 500/800 MW units of Dr NTTPS.
accepted.tq: Match the washery supply arrangement with both recipient stations and capacities.
accepted.sec: Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which State has the largest coal reserves in India according to the stated GSI estimate?
accepted.x: Jharkhand has the largest coal reserves among the States listed in the GSI estimate.
accepted.tq: Use the state ranking rather than confusing reserve concentration with production or lignite leadership.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: The GSI estimated India's coal resources at approximately what quantity as on 1 April 2024?
accepted.x: The GSI estimate placed India's coal resources at 389.421 billion tonnes as on 1 April 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current estimate from the older approximate figure.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the largest coking-coal field in India?
accepted.x: Jharia is identified as India's largest coking-coal field.
accepted.tq: Identify the field by its special classification rather than by its State alone.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Gondwana coal:
1. It is about 250–300 million years old.
2. It accounts for approximately 98% of India's coal reserves.
3. It contains the coking coal resources.
4. It occurs in the Damodar, Mahanadi, Son and Godavari valleys.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Gondwana coal is 250–300 million years old, constitutes about 98% of reserves, contains coking coal and occurs in the four stated valleys.
accepted.tq: Combine age, proportion, quality and geographic distribution in one classification question.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: Tertiary coal, which is generally associated with lignite, is approximately:
accepted.x: Tertiary coal is approximately 15–60 million years old and is associated with lignite.
accepted.tq: Contrast the age range of Tertiary coal with the much older Gondwana coal.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the reserve and leading-State position of lignite?
o: 15.000 billion tonnes; Rajasthan led by Singrauli
47.295 billion tonnes; Odisha led by Talcher
47.295 billion tonnes; Tamil Nadu led by Neyveli
389.421 billion tonnes; Jharkhand led by Jharia
accepted.x: Lignite resources are estimated at 47.295 billion tonnes, with Tamil Nadu leading through the Neyveli region, followed by Rajasthan and Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Match the resource figure with the correct leading State and field.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: Which of the following coalfield–State pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Raniganj is located in West Bengal. Talcher is in Odisha, Singrauli is in Madhya Pradesh and Makum is in Assam.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure location and eliminate swapped State associations.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: The first coal mine at Raniganj was established in 1774 at:
accepted.x: The first mine at the Raniganj coalfield was established in 1774 at Sitarampur.
accepted.tq: Link the historical date with the specific place within the coalfield.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs of coalfields is correctly associated with Odisha?
accepted.x: Talcher and Deogarh, including the IB Valley, are coalfields of Odisha. Jharia and Bokaro are in Jharkhand, Korba and Raigarh in Chhattisgarh, and Singareni and Makum in Telangana and Assam respectively.
accepted.tq: Group coalfields by State and reject cross-State substitutions.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: Which of the following coalfield–State pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Deogarh is in Odisha, not Madhya Pradesh. Jharia, Korba and Singareni are correctly associated with Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Telangana respectively.
accepted.tq: Find the single location swap among neighbouring coal-producing regions.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s: Approximately what proportion of India's coal reserves lies in the Damodar Valley?
accepted.x: About one-fourth of India's coal reserves lie in the Damodar Valley.
accepted.tq: Recall the fraction and distinguish it from broader regional descriptions.
accepted.sec: Coal reserves - state ranking and coalfields

accepted.s:
Arrange the following coal types in descending order of carbon content:
A. Lignite
B. Anthracite
C. Peat
D. Bituminous
E. Sub-bituminous
accepted.x: The descending order is anthracite, bituminous, sub-bituminous, lignite and peat.
accepted.tq: Arrange the grades by the carbon-content hierarchy, not by age or colour.
accepted.sec: Coal types - carbon content order

accepted.s: Which type of coal contains the highest carbon content, generally about 80–95%?
accepted.x: Anthracite contains approximately 80–95% carbon and is the best-quality coal.
accepted.tq: Match the highest carbon range with the highest-grade coal type.
accepted.sec: Coal types - carbon content order

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about anthracite is correct?
o: It is known as brown coal and is centred on Neyveli.
It is the first stage in the transformation of wood into coal.
Small amounts occur in Jammu and Kashmir.
It is found in large quantities throughout India.
accepted.x: Anthracite is found only in small amounts in Jammu and Kashmir. Peat is the first stage, while lignite is brown coal associated with places such as Neyveli.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive occurrence of anthracite to reject descriptions of other coal types.
accepted.sec: Coal types - carbon content order

accepted.s: Which type of coal is most widely used and is also the coking grade?
accepted.x: Bituminous coal is the most widely used type and includes the coking grade.
accepted.tq: Identify the coal type by its use and industrial grade.
accepted.sec: Coal types - carbon content order

accepted.s: Sub-bituminous coal is best described as coal that:
o: Is a brown coal found only in Jammu and Kashmir
Lies between bituminous coal and lignite and is used in power plants
Contains under 40% carbon and represents the first stage of coal formation
Contains 80–95% carbon and is the best-quality coal
accepted.x: Sub-bituminous coal lies between bituminous coal and lignite in rank and is used in power plants.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the intermediate coal type from both higher- and lower-rank varieties.
accepted.sec: Coal types - carbon content order

accepted.s: Lignite generally contains approximately what percentage of carbon and is also known as:
accepted.x: Lignite generally contains about 40–55% carbon and is commonly called brown coal.
accepted.tq: Pair the numerical range with the accepted descriptive name.
accepted.sec: Coal types - carbon content order

accepted.s: Which of the following set of places is associated with lignite occurrences mentioned in the classification?
accepted.x: Neyveli, Palana and Lakhimpur are identified with lignite occurrences. The other groups are associated with major coalfields of higher-rank coal regions.
accepted.tq: Recognise the lignite-location group instead of a group of Gondwana coalfields.
accepted.sec: Coal types - carbon content order

accepted.s: Peat is characterised by which of the following?
o: 60–80% carbon and use as coking coal
Less than 40% carbon and being the first stage in the transformation of wood into coal
40–55% carbon and occurrence mainly at Neyveli
accepted.x: Peat contains under 40% carbon and represents the first stage in the change from wood to coal.
accepted.tq: Use the defining formation-stage description to identify the lowest-rank material.
accepted.sec: Coal types - carbon content order
